key_insight: In a retrospective simulation, Sybil identified 33.8% of negative lung cancer screens for biennial screening with no delayed cancers observed.
clinical_relevance: AI-guided screening intervals could reduce radiology workload and expand screening capacity, pending prospective validation.
method: Retrospectively analyzed 3,120 lung cancer screenings from a tertiary safety-net hospital.
Externally evaluated Sybil, focusing on Lung-RADS 1–2 cases.
Simulated interval extension using Sybil and Brock risk scores calibrated on an NLST subset.
evidence_signal: Sybil achieved overall AUCs of 0.819–0.912 and a 2-year AUC of 0.746 in Lung-RADS 1–2 cases; 72 cancers occurred among 3,120 screenings.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective simulations with median follow-up of 2.3 years do not establish the safety of longer screening intervals in practice.
paper_title: Investigating AI's potential in risk-stratifying lung cancer screenings for extending screening intervals and reducing workload: A retrospective analysis of a tertiary hospital cohort
